resources.string: A full copy of the app: settings, device lists, LAN connections, cloud drives with sign-in, passwords and the ADB key. “Create backup” saves a dated file to the backup folder at once, “Restore…” lists the backups from that folder. The folder is changed with “Change…”: storage, SD card, USB, a network folder (SMB, SFTP, FTP, WebDAV) or a cloud.
Choose storage, a network source or a cloud
Wrong password. The file is not changed, try again.
The file is encrypted with the password (AES-256)
Encrypted with password: Android Backup, AES-256
Connection %1$s is not among the saved ones. Add it in Files or choose another place.
Clouds need the “ADB-phon Clouds” module: open a cloud in Files and the app offers to install it.
No access to folder %1$s: give the app access to all files (Settings, Apps, ADB-phon, All files access) or choose a network folder.
The file is empty or was not created
Written %1$d of %2$d bytes: the file is incomplete, the backup is not counted
Settings and backups with data (root or ADB needed)
Backups with data: apps from the last manual backup: %1$d
Backups with data: make one backup with data manually first, the auto backup takes the same apps
Backups with data skipped: root and ADB are not available now (noted in the log)
Root or ADB (wireless debugging) is needed. The connection failed: open the Link tab.
Format and moving to another device

The backup is saved as one .ab file in Android Backup format (AES-256 with a password). On a PC it opens with android-backup-extractor (java -jar abe.jar unpack file.ab file.tar password); inside is a tar with the backup parts. ADB-phon restores the data. Also inside: user, app version, Android version, model and app signature. Moving to another device: choose a network folder, a cloud or a USB drive, then on the other device open Backups with data, Restore from file….

Data goes back only into an installed app with the same signature. If the app is missing, install it first (the Install from backup button appears when the backup has the APK). Without root internal data is not restored, and the system backup (bu, adb restore) does not work for many apps on Android 12 and newer.
%1$s: the app is installed. Now the data can be restored.
The backup has no APK: install the app from a store, then restore the data
No root and no ADB: data cannot be restored. Connect ADB in the Link tab.
This user does not exist on this device: choose another one
The app is not installed for this user. Data is not restored without the app: install it first.
The installed app signature differs from the one in the backup: the data will not fit (another build of the same app)
Signature not checked (no signature info in the backup or on the device)
An older version is installed (code %2$s) than in the backup (%1$s): data of the newer version may not open. Better install the version from the backup first.
A newer version is installed than in the backup: the app usually upgrades old data itself
The backup was taken on Android %1$s, here Android API %2$s: data that depends on the system (notifications, permissions, keys) may not fit
The backup is from another device (%1$s): device-bound keys and account sign-ins may ask to sign in again
Internal data in the backup was taken with root: without root it is not restored, only the APK and external data come back
System backup: on Android 12 and newer without root the system may refuse the data of this app
The backup has only the APK, no data
